```{python}
#| label: setup

import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import cs_tables as C
import delta_figure as F
import laplacelib as R

SC = "022-laplace"
d = C.declared(C.load(SC))
sig = d.filter(~pl.col("null"))
```

Five logistic-SuSiE arms, all in the Gaussian family $\mathcal{Q}_2$ (see the
[pilot](results.qmd) for the arm definitions). Design: sparse 0/1 columns ($n = 1000$,
$p = 256$, adjacent-column $\phi = 0.8$), $b_0 = -2$, $L^* = 3$ causals at gap 8 (binary
$\phi \approx 0.47$ between causals) or 64 ($\phi \approx 0.05$), fit with $L = 5$. Axis:
expected set size $m$, with $\beta$ calibrated per $m$ to $E[\text{LRT}] = T$ so detectability
is matched and only the shape of each feature's likelihood changes with $m$.

All CS metrics are over **declared** CSs (component $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$). An undeclared
component has $\alpha$ near uniform and a 95% set of ~240 of 256 features, so its coverage is
1 by construction; pooling it in would erase every difference. The ranking of the arms is the
same at every $\log \text{BF}$ cut from 0 to 10.

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
n_cells = sig.select("T", "gap", "m").unique().height
reps = sig.group_by("T", "gap", "m", "method").len()["len"]
print(f"{SC}: {n_cells} signal cells x {sig['method'].n_unique()} arms, "
      f"{reps.min()}-{reps.max()} reps per cell; {d.filter(pl.col('null')).select('m').unique().height} null cells.")
```

# Along m {#sec-along-m}

## Relative to CAVI-Q2 {#sec-delta}

```{python}
#| label: fig-delta
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, relative to CAVI. Logistic SuSiE approximations are compared with CAVI-Q2 in the binary design experiment ($n = 1000$, $p = 256$, $\\rho = 0.8$, $L^* = 3$, fit $L = 5$, 200 replicates per cell). The x axis is the expected proportion of 1s in a column, $\\theta = P(X = 1)$; effect sizes are tuned per $\\theta$ so the expected log likelihood ratio of the causal variable against the null is $T$. Columns: signal strength ($T = 8, 16$) over the correlation between causal variables (gap 8 or 64 columns apart). Rows: coverage of declared 95% credible sets, power (fraction of causal variables captured by a declared set), and credible set size as the ratio of geometric means (log axis). Each arm is shown as its difference from CAVI-Q2 on the same replicates; the dashed line is no difference. Bands are 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
delta = F.delta_frame(d, ref="cavi")
F.draw(delta, ref="cavi");
```

## Absolute {#sec-absolute}

```{python}
#| label: fig-absolute
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, absolute. The same experiment and layout as above, with each arm's own coverage of declared 95% credible sets (dashed line: nominal 0.95), power, and geometric-mean credible set size (log axis). Bands are per-arm 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
absf = F.delta_frame(d, ref=None)
F.draw(absf, ref=None);
```

# Null cells {#sec-null}

```{python}
#| label: tab-null
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
nul = (d.filter(pl.col("null")).group_by(["m", "method"])
         .agg(pl.col("n_declared").mean().alias("false_cs"), pl.len().alias("reps")))
print("Declared CSs per fit on null data ($\\beta = 0$); every one is false. Reps in parentheses.\n")
print(C.table(nul, ["m"], "false_cs", lambda r: f"{r['false_cs']:.2f} ({int(r['reps'])})"))
```
